data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Silver salt of a sulfonamide

## Mechanism of action
- Silver ions bind bacterial DNA and cell membranes; sulfadiazine adds antibacterial action — broad spectrum including Pseudomonas and Candida

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Burns (partial-thickness) — prevents infection
- Infected leg ulcers and wounds (short term)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply 1–3 mm layer once or twice daily with sterile technique

## Adverse effects
- Transient leucopenia (in burns), argyria with prolonged large-area use, pseudoeschar, skin staining
- Sulfonamide hypersensitivity; haemolysis in G6PD deficiency; kernicterus (neonates)

## Contraindications
- Sulfonamide allergy; pregnancy at term, newborns under 2 months; G6PD deficiency (large areas)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid near term.

## Viva points
- Burn wound antimicrobial; leucopenia; avoid in newborns and late pregnancy

_Sources: Khopkar ch.18 and ch.32 (Wound care products); Wolverton 4e ch.54. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
